name: beech tree

attributes.attribute: one of the sacred trees of the Celts
a large tree of the genus Fagus that is kin to the oak
has a muscular gray trunk and a low full crown

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
The beech is one of the sacred trees of the Celts. This tree belongs to the genus Fagus. It stands as a large close kin of the oak. Its gray trunk looks thick and muscular. Its crown hangs low and full.

The beech held an honored place among the sacred plants of the Celts. Its wide branches cast a broad shade. Many a grove gave the tree its glory. The shape stayed low and full for the life of the tree.

okr.objective: Present the beech as a sacred tree of the Celtic world.
key_results: The beech stands among the sacred trees of the Celts.
It belongs to the genus Fagus and is kin to the oak.
It keeps a muscular gray trunk and a low, full crown.
